kind: actor runtime and standard systems libraries

runtime.execution: BEAM processes/mailboxes, distributed nodes, OTP state machines and native runtime.
runtime.service_boundary: Application/fabric machinery, not an agent; a harness may consume services without governing all nodes or databases.

summary: Message identity, explicit state migration and old/current code semantics are strong hot-change primitives, with sharp purge and runtime-replacement boundaries.

inspection.scope: Read module load/purge contract and entry functions, sys change/suspend dispatch, gen_server messaging, Mnesia transaction interface and soft-purge test.
inspection.limits: Native VM internals, full distributed protocols and Mnesia durability implementation not audited; no agent/provider path supplied.

actions.name: code:load_binary / soft_purge / purge
actions.lifecycle: Two code versions; destructive purge can terminate lingering processes.

actions.name: sys:suspend / change_code / resume
actions.input: Process, old version, extra migration data and timeout
actions.lifecycle: Suspend before migration; process identity persists.

actions.name: gen_server:cast
actions.lifecycle: Asynchronous mailbox delivery, not terminal work result.

actions.name: mnesia:transaction
actions.input: Executable function with table operations and retry policy
actions.lifecycle: Transaction lifetime; independent service ownership must be designed.

persistent_kernel.detail: Actor state remains while module code is migrated; VM restart does not automatically preserve it.

standing_database.detail: Mnesia transactional table operations are supplied primitives; exposure/ownership and independent durability remain separate design work.

workflow_programming.detail: Actor callbacks/state migration and custom event hooks support executable orchestration rather than fixed model workflow.

hot_change.detail: Explicit load plus suspended code_change migrates actor state; activation timing must be programmed, old frames may remain.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Live bytecode update preserves processes with deliberate state migration, but third-version purge can kill old-code users; replacement of the native VM itself is not supplied by module load.

remote_services.detail: Distributed named-node cast enables remote actor service consumption; exactly-once delivery or reconnect is not inferred.

authority.detail: Code load/debug/DB APIs operate with node/application authority; no agent approval policy.

evaluation.detail: Soft-purge test explicitly verifies refusal and target survival while code is referenced, then success after target termination.

time_order.detail: System/monotonic APIs distinguish time domains; monotonic bases cannot be compared across VM instances and ties occur.

evidence.claim: Old/current versions may coexist; third load can purge and kill old-code processes.
Binary code preparation and code-server load support in-process module replacement.
Purge kills lingering processes; soft_purge refuses when references remain.
System code change requires suspension and invokes explicit state migration callback.
Debug event hooks support trace, bounded event log and custom callback state; only supplied events are observed.
Cast dispatch can target named remote-node destination; asynchronous send returns ok.
Transactions compose table writes and return atomic result or abort; not model exposure by itself.
Monotonic times may tie and have incomparable bases across runtime instances.

tests.oracle: soft_purge returns false and process remains alive while referenced; returns true after process exits; not VM upgrade or agent continuity.

strengths: Code versions and state migration are explicit inspectable mechanisms.
Actor messaging, service supervision concepts and DB transactions can support programmable agents without JS.
limits: Asynchronous cast ok does not mean a recipient processed the message.
Live module upgrade is not native VM rebuild; purge and state-schema decisions remain dangerous if implicit.
arconaut_questions: Which program definitions need generation identity and explicit old-state migration?
Can refit require a settled request graph while allowing shared actors/services to continue for other consumers?
